TankieTube was a **five-day collaborative research sprint** at the University of Amsterdam. Our team compared "natively digital" Marxist-Leninist YouTube creators with formal political organizations.

**Team:** Luca Ghiselli, Ema Kinsel, Gavin Mueller, Ada Paul, Sean Ryan, and Jo Walton.

My part focused on the **Tenet/Rumble comparison**, and I also helped make the final poster. This was my first real hands-on exposure to Google Colab, very large text datasets, and computational internet research.

## Tenet/Rumble comparison

I found a public dataset of **560 Tenet Media videos on Rumble** and compared its transcripts with the much larger Tankie corpus.

- **TF-IDF** surfaced important words shared across both datasets.
- "Israel" became a focus, and a **sentence-similarity matcher** paired Tenet quotes with the closest Tankie quotes.

The goal was exploratory: find rhetorical overlap that would be hard to spot manually, not prove coordination.

## What the team found

The broader dataset covered **23 YouTube channels, nine political organizations, about 2.5 million comments, and more than 6,000 hours of audio**.

- The YouTubers and formal organizations focused on noticeably different topics.
- YouTubers appeared more shaped by platform dynamics, while organizations looked more like traditional social-movement activism.
- The team also found some aesthetic convergence between older organizations and newer YouTube-driven Marxism-Leninism.

## Why it mattered to me

Five days of working inside datasets that were far too large to read manually made computational research feel much more concrete. It helped push my interests toward digital investigations and data-driven online research.
